one_liner: Enterprise CRM platform with a very broad REST/SOAP/Bulk API surface.
auth_notes: REST API requires OAuth 2.0 via an external client app (new) or connected app (creation restricted since Spring '26); multiple flows incl. client credentials. Per search snippets; developer.salesforce.com docs returned HTTP 403 to fetch.
access_notes: Free Developer Edition org gives working API access (per Salesforce docs search snippet; page not fetchable).
api_notes: REST, SOAP, Bulk, Metadata, UI GraphQL APIs covering essentially all standard and custom objects (from prior knowledge; docs 403).
human_reason: developer.salesforce.com docs (OAuth, signup, hosted MCP) all returned HTTP 403; auth/access/API fields rest on search snippets and the archived salesforcecli/mcp repo (which also says EOL Nov 2 2026 in favor of hosted MCP servers).

one_liner: CRM and marketing platform with a broad REST API and an official remote MCP server.
auth_notes: OAuth 2.0 apps (access tokens expire in 30 min, refresh tokens). Static private-app/service-key bearer tokens exist per prior knowledge, not confirmed on fetched pages.
access_notes: Developer test accounts are free (90-day enterprise trial features); free HubSpot CRM accounts also work.
api_notes: Date-versioned REST APIs at api.hubapi.com (e.g. /crm/objects/2026-09/contacts) across CRM, marketing, CMS etc.

one_liner: Sales CRM with a REST API (v1/v2) and a native hosted MCP server.
auth_notes: OAuth 2.0 for apps; personal API token sent in x-api-token header (one per user/company).
access_notes: API token available from any account; a separate Developer Sandbox account can be requested (free status not stated on page). Trial accounts also give a token.
api_notes: ~50 endpoint groups (Deals, Leads, Persons, Organizations, Activities, Projects, Webhooks); OpenAPI specs for v1 and v2.

one_liner: Modern customizable CRM with a public REST API and an official hosted MCP server.
auth_notes: OAuth 2.0 auth-code (PKCE for user-level tokens) for multi-workspace apps; API key for single workspace; both sent as Bearer header.
access_notes: API key generated in developer settings; docs do not state plan requirements (Attio has a free plan - not confirmed on opened pages). Unpublished apps installable in up to 25 workspaces.
api_notes: Records, objects, lists, notes, tasks, comments, webhooks, meetings etc. with endpoint reference.

one_liner: Open-source, self-hostable CRM with REST and GraphQL APIs and built-in MCP.
auth_notes: Bearer API keys created in Settings > Developers > API (role-scoped); OAuth for external apps acting on behalf of users.
access_notes: Open source and self-hostable (Docker Compose) or Twenty Cloud at api.twenty.com; API key created in settings.
api_notes: Core API (CRUD on people, companies, custom objects) and Metadata API (schema), each in REST and GraphQL.

one_liner: Flexible work-management platform (now Progress) with a full REST API and a beta official MCP server.
auth_notes: OAuth2 with server-side, client-side, username/password and app-authentication flows; Client ID/Secret from API key page.
access_notes: Need a Podio account and generate an API key in account settings; whether a free tier still exists is not stated on opened pages (assumed trial/paid).
api_notes: Described as a complete programmable interface to all Podio functionality; webhooks; client libraries in many languages.

one_liner: Zoho's CRM suite with a versioned REST API and built-in official MCP servers.
auth_notes: OAuth 2.0 only; Client ID/Secret from a connected app (Zoho API console); access tokens last 1 hour, refresh tokens persist.
access_notes: Free edition exists with 5,000 API credits per 24h and 5 concurrent calls; trial editions share paid-edition limits.
api_notes: Six families: Metadata, Core CRUD, Composite, Bulk, Notification, Query (COQL).

one_liner: Sales CRM for SMBs with REST API and an official hosted MCP server.
auth_notes: API key from Settings > Developer sent as HTTP Basic (key as username); OAuth2 for integrations.
access_notes: API keys created by any user in account settings; Close is paid with a free trial (trial terms not stated on opened pages).
api_notes: REST API plus webhooks, event log, reporting, sequences, bulk actions.

one_liner: Google Workspace-native CRM with a REST developer API.
auth_notes: API key (user token plus user email headers) generated in System settings > API Keys; OAuth 2.0 preferred for partner integrations.
access_notes: Key generated in-app; docs do not state plan requirements; Copper is paid with a trial (not confirmed on opened pages).
api_notes: Leads, People, Companies, Opportunities, Projects, Tasks, Activities, Custom Fields, Webhooks.

one_liner: Intapp DealCloud enterprise CRM with REST API, SDKs and an official MCP server.
auth_notes: OAuth2 client-credentials flow (scopes data, user_management, publish, ri_import, backup; 15-min tokens) using per-user API key enabled in profile.
access_notes: Enterprise product; an admin must grant the user group API capability; no self-serve trial/sandbox found - needs an existing customer tenant.
api_notes: REST at {baseUrl}/api/rest/v1 with Python and C# SDKs; data, user management, publish, backup scopes.

one_liner: Help desk / service platform with a very broad REST API across Support, Help Center, Sell and more.
auth_notes: OAuth access tokens (recommended; global OAuth client for multi-customer apps); API tokens via Basic auth (email/token:token) are marked deprecated.
access_notes: 14-day free trial; API tokens created in Admin Center > APIs; OAuth clients created by admins. Plan requirements not stated.
api_notes: Ticketing, Help Center, Messaging, Voice, Custom Data, Sell CRM, Apps and more APIs.
human_reason: Zendesk's own MCP server status is contradictory: an opened Oct 2026 article says announced but no public docs; search results claim early access opened Nov 10 2026 (not verifiable on developer.zendesk.com). Marked community pending confirmation.

one_liner: Customer messaging/support platform with REST API and an official hosted MCP server.
auth_notes: Access token for private apps (Developer Hub > Configure > Authentication); OAuth for public apps.
access_notes: Create an app in Developer Hub via developer signup to get a token for your workspace; pricing of the dev workspace not stated on opened page (assumed free test workspace).
api_notes: Conversations, contacts, companies, articles etc. (MCP scopes show read/write across these).

one_liner: Freshworks help desk with a broad v2 REST API and an official MCP endpoint (GA Sept 2026).
auth_notes: Personal API key as Basic-auth username (password X); OAuth scopes exist but flow not described on opened page.
access_notes: API key from profile settings; trial accounts limited to 50 calls/min; rate limits and some features vary by plan. Free trial assumed from prior knowledge.
api_notes: Tickets, contacts, companies, agents, solutions, forums, SLA, automations, custom objects, CSAT etc.

one_liner: Shared inbox and customer ops platform with a REST Core API.
auth_notes: Admin-created company API tokens (Settings > Developers) sent as Bearer; OAuth authorization-code required for public integrations. MCP server scope not available to API tokens.
access_notes: Only admins can create tokens; no plan requirement stated; paid product with trial (trial not confirmed on opened pages).
api_notes: Core API for conversations, contacts, inboxes, rules, tags, teams, accounts (api2.frontapp.com) per search summary; token scope page confirms core resources.
human_reason: Front's token page references an 'MCP server' scope (implying an official MCP server) but I did not open an MCP doc page or find its URL; main API docs fetch returned 404.

one_liner: B2B support platform with a REST API (SDKs in TS/Python/Go) and an official OAuth-only hosted MCP.
auth_notes: Admin-created Bearer API tokens (Settings > Integrations & dev > API), region-specific, non-expiring; MCP is OAuth-only.
access_notes: Need an existing Pylon tenant and an Admin to create tokens; no self-serve signup or plan info found.
api_notes: Issues, accounts, contacts and more; TS/Python/Go SDKs and experimental CLI; breadth inferred from docs summary.
blocker: no self-serve signup; need paying/sales-onboarded tenant
human_reason: Could not find any page stating how a new developer gets a Pylon tenant or plan requirements for API/trial.

one_liner: Help desk platform with API v3 (key-based) and an official MCP integration.
auth_notes: API v3 uses an apikey parameter; MCP supports OAuth 2.1 or Bearer token (up to 10 tokens, 2-year expiry).
access_notes: Key created in agent panel; docs opened do not state plan requirements or trial terms (trial assumed from prior knowledge).
api_notes: API v3 with scoped keys; breadth not confirmed from opened pages.

one_liner: API-first B2B support tool with a GraphQL API (no UI/API gap) and official OAuth MCP.
auth_notes: API keys (Bearer) created on machine users with per-permission scopes; OAuth app for acting as a user.
access_notes: Key created in Settings > Machine users & agents; plan requirements not stated on opened pages.
api_notes: Docs state no limitations in API vs UI; GraphQL schema.

one_liner: Shared inbox/help desk with Inbox API 2.0 (OAuth2) and an official read-only hosted MCP.
auth_notes: Authorization-code flow for public integrations; client-credentials for internal; create app in Profile > My apps.
access_notes: Any user with API access can create an app; docs state no plan requirement for API (MCP needs Standard/Plus/Pro). Trial assumed from prior knowledge.
api_notes: Conversations, customers, inboxes, organizations, reports, tags, users/teams, workflows, webhooks.

one_liner: E-commerce help desk with a REST API and first-party hosted MCP (open beta).
auth_notes: Private apps use API key (Basic with email + key); public apps must use OAuth2.
access_notes: Credentials from account settings; docs fetched do not explain obtaining keys or plans (trial assumed). MCP works on any plan.
api_notes: Resource-oriented JSON REST API with full reference; undocumented resources are internal.

one_liner: Enterprise customer-service platform with a REST API using per-user API tokens (Basic auth).
auth_notes: Agent email as username and API token as password; token created in More settings > API Tokens by a user with API User permission.
access_notes: Enterprise product, no self-serve trial or free tier found; an admin of an existing Gladly tenant must grant API User permission.
api_notes: Agents, conversations, customers, tasks, topics, inboxes, reports, webhooks, data exports, etc.
